content:
alex: heads-up, seeing sustained tail latency and queue growth in shared-gpu-pool(us-west1) starting ~02:15 UTC. top offenders look like tenant:ml-training-42 and tenant:search-proto.

maria: grim. are they both bursty inference or long-running decodes?

alex: mostly long decodes with large context. p95 tokens/sec drops and KV cache thrashing. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/8Gk/queueing?orgId=1&var-pool=shared-gpu-pool

jordan: i can confirm spike. node-level GPU mem pressure + >3m pending queue. cpu+io also spiking on sidecars.

priya: quick mitigation: reduce per-tenant max_concurrency and apply a short token-bucket on the edge. i can push a proxy rule. anyone opposed?

sam: +1 on proxy cap. also we should avoid hard evictions — prefer soft backpressure and tenant shaping.

alex: agree. can we try: max_concurrency=8, rate=2rps burst=4 for the noisy tenants. then watch tail latency for small tenants.

maria: can we target only those tenant ids? we have routing metadata for tenant weights.

priya: yes, can patch route-match for tenant labels. snippet below for the envoy route (canary):

```
route_match:
  headers:
    - name: x-tenant-id
      exact_match: "ml-training-42"
rate_limits:
  - stage: 0
    actions:
      - generic_key:
          descriptor_value: "ml-training-42-shape"
          header_name: "x-tenant-id"
```

priya: will push canary to 4 proxies now, watch metrics for 10m. infra-bot: roll-canary start for tenant shaping (canary-id: cs-1849)

infra-bot: deployed canary cs-1849 to proxies: p-12,p-15,p-18,p-22 — monitoring enabled.

jordan: FYI we also have a backlog in the scheduler's admission queue. if queueing policy is FIFO then a single noisy tenant blocks others. suggestion: enable per-tenant fair-queue slotting (N slots per tenant, global slot pool).

sam: how expensive is that change? needs scheduler work and maybe oncall window.

jordan: small config-first change exists: `per_tenant_slots_enabled=true` toggles slot accounting. it defaults false. enable in staging today, prod tomorrow if metrics look good.

alex: actionable plan: 1) priya pushes proxy rate caps for top offenders (in progress) 2) enable per_tenant_slots in staging (jordan) 3) add temporary canary routing of ml-training-42 to dedicated pool if caps don't help (costy) 4) follow-up postmortem if regression.

maria: add a dashboard panel for "blocked_by_noisy_tenant" — set alert for >5% of requests queued >120s.

priya: canary metrics: 10m in, dropped qlen by ~60% on canaryed proxies; overall cluster pending down ~18%. tail latency p99 still elevated on GPU nodes, likely due to in-flight decodes.

alex: thanks. if p99 doesn't come down after 30m we should route offending tenant to dedicated pool as an emergency (will notify sales).

jordan: i'll kick off staging toggle now. command: `./opsctl feature-flag set per_tenant_slots true --env=staging`

infra-bot: staging toggle succeeded. watching metrics.

sam: one more thought: enable short-lived soft-preempt (preempt oldest slot requests from heavy tenants) vs hard kill. less user-visible. add to playbook?

alex: yes add to playbook. can someone own the follow-up? @maria?

maria: i'll own the follow-up. will collect traces, scheduler histograms, and cost delta if we spin up dedicated capacity.

priya: can we also log tenant request sizes so we can auto-suggest quantization/trim prompts? small win for long decodes.

alex: good idea. add an internal event: `tenant_request_size` with approximate token count (no PII).

maria: created incident ticket IN-1849 and linked this thread. I'll update as we see changes.

infra-bot: incident IN-1849 created by maria at 02:33 UTC.

alex: thanks all — keep updates short here. if anyone needs to escalate to infra oncall, ping channel @oncall.
